newsitem.title: UK: Grandmet/Guinness deal signals drinks "big bang".
newsitem.headline: Grandmet/Guinness deal signals drinks "big bang".

text.p: The merger between Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc has signalled a "big bang" in the consumer industry which is bound to unnerve rivals like Allied Domecq and Seagram, analysts said.
"This is a big bang for the spirits industry after the last consolidation ten years ago," said Ron Littleboy, analyst at Nomura.

"It's great news for both companies, all the others will be worried sick, but what are they to do -- this group is now just so powerful and there is unlikely to be a deal open to others which offers the same scale of benefits."
Ten years ago Guinness bought United Distillers, GrandMet acquired Heublein and Allied Lyons bought Hiram Walker.
Analysts said the Guinness merger with GrandMet greatly weakened the position of drinks and retail group Allied Domecq Plc ALLD L, due to report its half year results on Tuesday.
"It presents a tremendously difficult problem for Allied," said Philip Hawkins, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"They will have to look for strategic partners otherwise they will continue to see their market share erode further and continue to underperform," he said.
The most Allied can hope for is to sew up a deal with Seagram Co Ltd VO.TO or fall subject to a predator, possibly the likes of American Brands Inc AMB.N or Brown-Forman Corp BFa.N, analysts said.
"Allied and Seagram and Pernod will all be very worried. It could be the last nail in the coffin for Allied, they will have to do something dramatic now," said Littleboy.
